Let Assumption \ref{main assumption convergence rate} be satisfied.

The constants $C$ appearing in these theorems can depend on $T$, $[f]_{L}$, $[f]_{H}$, $\norm{\partial_{(y,z)}^{1} f}$ and $L$.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorems are asserted under Assumption 1 alone (f Lipschitz, ξ ∈ L^2). Their (unwritten) proof combines Theorem 'main convergence rate', which requires Assumption 'main assumption convergence rate' (ξ ∈ D^{2,q}, q>4, Hölder Malliavin derivative, f ∈ C^{1:2}, time-Hölder f) and |π|<η, with Lemma 'error implementation' (|π| small), Lemma 'truncation order chaos' (needs f_i ∈ D^{1,2}) and Lemma 'malliavin-energy' (needs f ∈ C^{1:1}_{b,(y,z)}). Under Assumption 1 alone, E(‖Dξ‖²) in the bound is not even defined, the O(|π|) rate is not available, and the smallness of |π| is not imposed. Thus the statement is not supported by the invoked results as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'Let Assumption 1 be satisfied' by Assumption 'main assumption convergence rate' (which already implies f ∈ C^{1:1}_{b,(y,z)} and ξ ∈ D^{1,2}) and add 'for |π| sufficiently small'; the combination argument then goes through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Both main error estimates (Theorems thm:added-4 and thm:added-5) are unestablished in the stated generality; they only hold under the stronger regularity assumptions actually used by the ingredients and for |π| small.
issues.title: Main error theorems stated under Assumption 1 only, but their derivation needs the Malliavin/Hölder regularity of Assumption 2.x, f ∈ C^{1:1}_{b,(y,z)} and a small-mesh condition
issues.why_classification: The fix is to state the hypotheses that the cited ingredients already require; the method, rates and conclusions all survive with no new argument.

issues.failure_explanation: By construction Y^{π,θ}_{t_{i-1}} + ∫_{t_{i-1}}^{t_i} Z^{π,θ} dB = C^{θ(i)}(F_i^{π,θ}) = Y_{t_i}^{π,θ} + Δ_i C^P(f_i^{π,θ}), not Y_{t_i}^{π,θ} + Δ_i f_i^{π,θ}. The proof differentiates the wrong identity, so the term Δ_i D_s f_i^{π,θ} appearing in the derived equation is not what actually appears; the correct term is Δ_i D_s C^P(f_i^{π,θ}) = Δ_i C^{P-1}(D_s f_i^{π,θ}). The subsequent estimates are only justified once one notes E‖D C^P(f_i)‖² = E‖C^{P-1}(D f_i)‖² ≤ E‖D f_i‖², which the proof never does.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace f_i^{π,θ} by C^P(f_i^{π,θ}) in the differentiated identity and add the one-line bound E‖D C^P(f_i^{π,θ})‖²_{H_{t_i}} ≤ E‖D f_i^{π,θ}‖²_{H_{t_i}} via Lemma 'proposition inequality chaos truncation'(ii) and Lemma 'lemma norm malliavin'; the rest of the argument is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Lemma lem:malliavin-energy contains an incorrect step; the stated estimates (and their use in Theorems thm:added-4/thm:added-5) are nevertheless recoverable.
issues.title: Proof of the Malliavin energy estimate differentiates the untruncated recursion Y_{t_{i-1}}+∫Z dB = Y_{t_i}+Δ_i f_i, which the scheme does not satisfy
issues.why_classification: A short local correction using results already in the paper restores the proof with the same constants and conclusion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Notice that for a general square-integrable random variable $F$, the quantity $\mathbf{V}_i (F)$ can still be infinite.

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption 1 only requires ξ ∈ L²(F_T); square-integrability does not imply fourth moments, and the paper itself notes that V_i(F) may be infinite for a general square-integrable F. Counterexample: ξ = g(B(h_1)) with g²φ ~ 1/(x log² x) at infinity is in L² but E[ξ² H_1(B(h_1))²] = ∞, so V_m(ξ) = ∞. Hence the remark's inference is false as written; finiteness of V_m(ξ) needs a higher-moment (e.g. L^q, q>4, as in Assumption 'main assumption convergence rate') hypothesis.

failure_location.quote: Under Assumption \ref{assumption 1}, the random variable $\xi$ has absolute moments of fourth order, and hence $\mathbf{V}_{m}(\xi)$ can be proven to be finite.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'Under Assumption 1' by a hypothesis giving ξ ∈ L^4 (e.g. Assumption 'main assumption convergence rate', which gives ξ ∈ L^q, q>4), under which E[ξ²H_a²] < ∞ and V_m(ξ) < ∞ follow by Cauchy–Schwarz.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the Monte Carlo constant C_{P,M} in Theorem thm:added-5 is automatically finite under Assumption 1 is unsupported; the bound may be vacuous without an extra moment assumption on ξ.
issues.title: False claim that Assumption 1 yields fourth moments of ξ and finiteness of V_m(ξ)
issues.why_classification: Correcting the assumption cited in the remark is a local change; no result's proof or rate is altered.
